issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement explicitly instructs that Farm should aggregate animals using a List implemented as an ArrayList, but the solution implementation declares the field as Set<Animal> and initializes it with a HashSet. The template does not provide the field (left as a TODO) so students following the problem text will implement a List/ArrayList, yet the reference solution uses a different collection type (Set/HashSet). This mismatch changes ordering and duplicate-handling semantics and can confuse students about the required type and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the exercise specification: change the Farm.animals field and its getter/setter in the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>(), and update any iteration code accordingly. Alternatively, if using a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly permit a Set and document the changed semantics (no ordering, no duplicates). Prefer updating the solution to List/ArrayList to match the written task.

issues.description: Concept: the Farm's collection of animals. Problem statement explicitly requires a List implementation and instructs to "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments" (calls it a List/ArrayList). Template Farm.java contains a TODO and no concrete collection declaration (so students are told to use an ArrayList). The solution implements the collection as a Set with declaration "private Set<Animal> animals;" and instantiates a HashSet. This is an identifier/type inconsistency for the same conceptual entity (the animals collection) across artifacts: problem asks for List/ArrayList, template guides that way, but solution uses Set/HashSet. A student following the problem text or template would expect List<Animal> and ArrayList but would see a Set-based solution; getter/setter signatures and constructor initialization differ, increasing cognitive load and possibly causing confusion about required API and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent. Preferred fix: update the solution to use List<Animal> for the field and public getter/setter (change "private Set<Animal> animals" to "private List<Animal> animals"), instantiate it in the no-arg constructor as "new ArrayList<>()", and update getAnimals()/setAnimals() signatures to return/accept List<Animal>. Alternatively, relax the problem text to accept any Collection implementation (remove the explicit ArrayList/ArrayList-initialization instruction) if a Set is intended.
